{category}geography.short_description: Geographic FIPS code as a string: 5-digit county code in county_determinants.parquet; 2-digit state code or '00' (national) in state_determinants.parquet. Includes Puerto Rico (72) and, for AHRF only, Guam (66) and the U.S. Virgin Islands (78) where the source reports them.

{category}time.short_description: Year-end date (YYYY-12-31) of the data vintage. Each source has its own vintage(s): HUD CHAS 2022 (ACS 5-year), AHRF 1999-2025, BLS LAUS 2025, USDA Food Access Research Atlas 2019.

bundle_county_access/dist/county_determi.short_description: Identifier of the measure in this row; the name matches the source column in the contributing source's standard file.

bundle_county_access/dist/state_determin.short_description: Identifier of the measure in this row; the name matches the source column in the contributing source's standard file. USDA food access is county-only and does not appear in this file.

{category}value.long_name: Value of the determinant measure identified by outcome_name
{category}value.short_description: Value for the measure identified by the `outcome_name` column. Units differ by measure: HUD, BLS and USDA measures are proportions (0-1); AHRF measures are counts, rates, codes, or percentages as documented for each source variable.
{category}value.long_description: Value for the measure identified by the `outcome_name` column, taken unchanged from the contributing source's standard file (see each level's source documentation for definition and unit). Rows with missing values are dropped, so sparse AHRF measures have fewer rows than the full county x year grid. Note that `ahrf_rural_urban_code` is a categorical USDA Rural-Urban Continuum Code (1-9) stored numerically.

chr.name: County Health Rankings & Roadmaps
chr.organization: University of Wisconsin Population Health Institute
chr.location: County Health Rankings & Roadmaps Annual Data
chr.description: The County Health Rankings & Roadmaps (CHR&R) program, a collaboration between the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation and the University of Wisconsin Population Health Institute, ranks the health of nearly all counties in the nation. The annual rankings measure vital health factors including high school graduation rates, obesity, smoking, unemployment, access to healthy foods, the quality of air and water, income inequality, and teen births that influence how long and how well we live. Data are released annually and cover all U.S. counties. Raw data are publicly available through the Zenodo repository (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18157681) and span release years 2010 through the present.
